historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors
history.scopeNote: Basis scope: diphenhydramine-to-nisoxetine; extension to atomoxetine inferred.

starting.description: In the documented Lilly founding branch, diphenhydramine's observed potentiation of noradrenaline and inhibition of monoamine uptake suggested antidepressant potential and led to analogue synthesis and testing that yielded selective nisoxetine. Earlier observed neuronal uptake and imipramine's inhibition provided wider context. Documented class support is bounded to this founding branch; its extension to atomoxetine is inferred and the initial analogue-selection chronology remains unknown.

inspiration.description: Neuronal noradrenaline uptake and its inhibition by the existing antidepressant imipramine and the antihistamine diphenhydramine.

steps.description: Researchers observed neuronal uptake of noradrenaline and its inhibition by an existing antidepressant.
A separate early selective-noradrenaline inhibitor effort produced maprotiline.

Diphenhydramine's observed monoamine-uptake inhibition informed Lilly analogue synthesis; screening and structure-activity analysis produced nisoxetine, which was tested for selective noradrenaline uptake inhibition.

A 1982 original study reported selective norepinephrine uptake inhibition by LY139603, the more potent negative isomer of a phenoxypropylamine racemate. A later paper identifies LY139603 as atomoxetine, and a review describes its structural relationship to nisoxetine; these sources do not establish the exact development sequence between the compounds.

design.description: Researchers synthesized and screened diphenhydramine analogues, used structure-activity analysis to identify selective nisoxetine, and later compared the uptake inhibition of the optical isomers of a related methylphenoxy analogue. The precise rationale and chronological synthesis steps for selecting atomoxetine are not established by the sources read.

circumstances.description: The Lilly analogue synthesis and mouse and uptake testing were planned; this does not establish whether the earlier pharmacological observations were anticipated.

limits: Iversen describes an early selective maprotiline branch, not a direct chemical lineage to the Lilly program.

The diphenhydramine-to-nisoxetine founding program is documented; the extension of its observation-led origin to atomoxetine is inferred from a reported structural relationship and identity, not an explicit account of the precise synthesis sequence.
This record does not establish the distinct founding history of every selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor or the causal molecular mechanism of atomoxetine's ADHD effects.
gaps: Full texts of the 1982 original LY139603 experiment and 2002 atomoxetine experiment were inaccessible; abstracts only were read.
The initial diphenhydramine uptake observation and original nisoxetine work were not read in their original reports.

A contemporaneous account establishing why and in what chronological sequence the methylphenoxy analogue was selected for synthesis was not found; structural analogy alone does not prove a direct nisoxetine-to-atomoxetine optimization sequence.
